documents.post_award_reporting:
{
  "doc_id": "post_award_reporting",
  "title": "Post-Award — Reporting",
  "category": "post_award",
  "subcategory": "reporting",
  "display_label": "Reporting (Post-Award)",
  "source_url": "https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/post-award/reporting",
  "procedure_url": "https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/post-award/reporting",
  "content": "Reporting Overview. After an award is issued, funding agencies monitor both programmatic and financial aspects of a project. PIs/PDs prepare technical (programmatic) reports submitted to funding agencies at intervals specified in the Notice of Award (NoA) — monthly, quarterly, annually, or at grant closeout. The Office of Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA) handles fiscal reports; PIs are responsible for verifying the accuracy of expenses.\n\nCommon report types:\n- Programmatic: annual progress reports, final technical reports, invention reports, property/equipment reports.\n- Financial: annual financial reports, final financial reports, invoicing.\n\nProgrammatic Reporting Requirements: Final reports are normally due within 90 days after the end of the project period, and usually include the technical, property (major equipment), and invention reports. Report categories include Interim/Progress reports, Final Technical Reporting, Invention Reporting, and Final Reports / Closeout.\n\nEffort Reporting and Certification:\n- Schedule: Effort certifications are generated three times per year — February (Fall semester), July (Spring semester), and October (Summer effort).\n- Deadline: Once released to campus, certifications must be completed within 14 calendar days.\n- Platform: Searchlight.\n- Who must certify: All PIs/PDs, faculty, professional staff, and students paid directly from federal grants and contracts.\n- Definition: Effort is the amount of time spent on a particular activity. It includes time working on a sponsored project where salary is directly charged or cost-shared effort (also known as match).\n\nCost Sharing: Cost sharing represents that portion of the total project costs of a sponsored agreement that are not charged to the sponsor. These costs are absorbed by the University rather than by the sponsor.\n\nCompliance framework: All reporting is governed by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidelines, including 2 CFR 200 (Uniform Guidance).\n\nReferences: PI Handbook 5: Policies & Guidelines (PDF) — Effort Reporting on page 96, Cost Sharing on page 36. URL: https://www.morgan.edu/Documents/ADMINISTRATION/OFFICES/ora/PI/2024-07-01_PIHandbook5.pdf. PI Handbook 3: Grant-Related Processes (2025-02-24) covers post-award report mechanics.\n\nAdditional details (Programmatic Reporting accordion): Property and Invention reports must be completed even when the project acquired no equipment and produced no invention. PIs should treat the requirement seriously — failure to submit reports on time may adversely affect future prospects for funding from the agency. The schedule for required technical reports is typically incorporated in the award document from the sponsor.\n\nAdditional details (Effort Reporting accordion): Effort certifications cover employees paid from federal AND state contracts or grants, including any mandatory cost sharing accounts. PIs/PDs (or their approved designee, called an 'alternate certifier') must verify and certify the reports, attesting that employees actually performed the work on the indicated accounts in the same percentage of time. Any corrections to effort should be reported immediately to the ORA Director (Gillian.Silver@morgan.edu) and to the Grant Accountant assigned to the grant in Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA). PIs/PDs and alternate certifiers are notified via email from the Searchlight platform when reports are available. The electronic effort report may be certified by the employee, supervisor, or PI/PD who has personal familiarity with the employee's compensated effort. The report is after-the-fact and is generated from historical payroll data.\n\nAdditional details (Cost Sharing): Cost sharing can be required by the sponsor or volunteered by a PI/PD; regardless, any commitment of effort referenced in the project proposal or award document must be honored, reported, and captured in the effort reporting system. Because faculty, administrative, and clerical salaries at MSU are paid by the employee's department, cost-shared effort represents a redirection of departmental resources from teaching or other departmental activities to support sponsored agreements.\n\nKey contacts:\n- Ms. Gillian Silver, Director — Gillian.Silver@morgan.edu\n- Mr. Ryan Mobley, Training Coordinator — Ryan.Mobley@morgan.edu\n- General: 443-885-4044, ask.ora@morgan.edu, Tyler Hall Suite 304, Baltimore, MD 21251.",
  "last_scraped": "2026-05-14",
  "playwright_verified": true,
  "playwright_verified_at": "2026-05-14",
  "key_facts": {
    "final_report_due_days_after_project_end": 90,

{
  "doc_id": "pre_award_budget_development",
  "title": "Pre-Award — Budget Development",
  "category": "pre_award",
  "subcategory": "budget",
  "display_label": "Budget Development (Pre-Award)",
  "source_url": "https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/pre-award/budget-development",
  "procedure_url": "https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/pre-award/budget-development",
  "content": "Comprehensive guidance for preparing the budget (also called the cost proposal) for a Morgan State University sponsored project. ORA emphasizes that the budget is equally as important as the technical proposal. For questions contact ask.ora@morgan.edu or 443-885-4044 (fax 443-885-8280).

Budget overview: Budgets are comprehensive planning documents integrating details for achieving proposal objectives, accounting for both long-range goals and short-term targets. A budget typically includes direct costs, other direct costs, indirect costs, and other budget elements.

Expense categories:

Personnel salaries and wages: senior personnel, post-doctoral researchers, lab technicians, graduate/undergraduate students, teaching assistants, and clerical staff.

Fringe benefits (current rates): Regular full-time/non-contractual employees (year round) = 42% of gross salary; Faculty during academic year = 42%; Faculty during summer = 9%; Contractual employees (year round) = 9%. See the Fringe Benefit Rate page for the official rate letter.

Equipment: defined as property with acquisition cost of $5,000 or more and an expected service life exceeding one year. Brief descriptions and justifications are required.

Travel: includes domestic and international travel for fieldwork and conferences. Current 2025 reimbursable rates under the State of Maryland include personal automobile mileage at $0.70 per mile, and meal per diems of $15 (breakfast), $18 (lunch), and $30 (dinner) for a total of $63 daily. GSA Per Diem Rates and the MSU University Travel page are also referenced.

Participant support: costs that defray expenses for students in training activities, conferences, or symposiums. Participants must be non-MSU employees receiving services (not providing them). Morgan employees do not qualify as participants, and indirect costs are not allowed on participant support.

Materials and supplies: supplies, printing, instructional materials, and audiovisual/computer supplies.

Consultant services: require descriptions of proposed services, time estimates, and payment rates. MSU faculty may not be listed as consultants.

Subawards (also called subgrants, subagreements, or subcontracts): require clear budget provisions, separate identification, and a service explanation. See the Pre-Award Subawards page.

Facilities and Administrative (F&A) / Indirect Cost: Morgan State's currently negotiated rate for Organized Research (On-Campus) is 53%-54% of modified total direct cost (see the F&A Cost Rates page for the full rate schedule by fiscal year and activity type).

Linked templates and resources from this page: PI Handbook 2 (Grant Budgets) PDF, NSF Budget Template (protected Excel), Budget Justification Template (Word), and Budget Preparation PowerPoint Slides PDF.",

  "content": "The Internal Routing Form (IRF) is a required document that must be submitted before applying for any external funding, preferably two weeks prior to the sponsor's submission deadline. The IRF gives the Office of Research Administration basic information about the Principal Investigator and the funding opportunity, captures certifications regarding Responsible Conduct of Research standards, and confirms supervisory approval to proceed with the project. The IRF must collect signatures from the PI/PD, Department Chair, Dean or Center Director, ORA Research Budget Specialist, Grants Manager, and Director of Research Administration.\n\nDocuSign links:\n- PowerForm: https://powerforms.docusign.net/d952f118-fd7b-4b18-b238-57855dc939f7?env=na2&acct=91e00bed-fb84-48ab-9c47-f3a2c0621225&accountId=91e00bed-fb84-48ab-9c47-f3a2c0621225\n- Complete new IRF: https://na2.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=d952f118-fd7b-4b18-b238-57855dc939f7&env=na2&acct=91e00bed-fb84-48ab-9c47-f3a2c0621225&v=2",

  "doc_id": "pre_award_proposal_components",
  "title": "Pre-Award — Proposal Components",
  "category": "pre_award",
  "subcategory": "overview",
  "display_label": "Proposal Components (Pre-Award)",
  "source_url": "https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/pre-award/proposal-components",
  "procedure_url": "https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/pre-award/proposal-components",
  "content": "Technical components typically required for a research proposal at Morgan State University. ORA emphasizes that each Funding Opportunity Announcement (FoA) has specific requirements, so applicants must thoroughly review the relevant FoA before drafting. Contact ORA at ask.ora@morgan.edu or 443-885-4044 (fax 443-885-8280) for assistance.

Standard proposal components:

Abstract / Executive Summary: A concise summary written within sponsor-specified space limits, covering the problem, objectives, approach, and project cost. The abstract should be clear and should accurately reflect and parallel the content of the proposal.

Introduction / Background: Demonstrates knowledge of the field, identifies research gaps, and establishes project importance while relating specific aims to broader long-term goals.

Goals & Objectives: Specifies broad long-term goals and expected outcomes, followed by clear, brief, realistic, and measurable specific objectives.

Methodology: Explains how objectives will be achieved, relating the proposed approach to specific objectives and justifying the selection of methods.

Key Personnel: Describes qualifications, relevant experience, and specific roles of all key personnel. List the Principal Investigator first. Include any personnel critical to project success even if their salary is not being requested from the sponsor.

Evaluation: For training or demonstration projects, the evaluation section relates evaluation methods to stated objectives and describes data collection, timelines, resources, and intended use of results.",

  "content": "The Morgan State University Office of Research Administration (ORA) offers a comprehensive trainings program covering all aspects of administrative functions related to research at the university. The trainings page describes offerings as covering 'All Aspects of Administrative Functions at Morgan State University' and includes faculty/staff development videos, presentations, and workshops on research administration subjects.\n\nThe ORA training catalog is organized into the following seven sections, each with its own subpage:\n\n1) e-Training (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/trainings/e-training) — A gamut of self-paced eTraining modules touching on all aspects of administrative functions: Post Award Quick Guide; Navigating Banner: Essentials for Research Administration; Building the Project Team (contractual hiring, summer contracts, honoraria); Travel on Sponsored Projects; Purchasing with Purpose (procurement, Banner Pool Level 08, subawards); Supporting Participants (stipends, tuition, MTDC); Show Your Work (time and effort reporting); It Takes a Village (cost share).\n\n2) Research Compliance and Security Training (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/research-compliance/research-security/research-compliance-and-security-training) — REQUIRED for all MSU personnel engaged in federally funded research. Options include CITI Program (https://citiprogram.org/), NSF SECURE Center (https://www.secure-center.org/ctm), and NSF Modules (https://www.nsf.gov/research-security/training). Personnel must complete one approved option and retain the certificate.\n\n3) New Faculty Development Seminars (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/trainings/new-faculty-development-seminars) — Seminar series for new faculty covering the grant lifecycle, funding sources, proposal components, research/fiscal compliance, pedagogy, AI in research, the history of Morgan, and professional societies/fellowships. Presenters include Dr. Farin Kamangar, Gillian Silver, Laura Dorsey-Elson, Dr. Edet Isuk, and Dr. Edwin Johnson.\n\n4) Monthly D-RED Seminars (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/trainings/monthly-d-red-seminars) — Recurring monthly seminars on research administration topics. The pattern is typically the second Wednesday of each month (recent dates include Sep 10, Oct 9, Nov 12, Dec 11). Topics range from NSF funding strategy and CAREER awards, to research security, cost sharing, audits, intellectual property, export controls, conflict of interest, and time and effort reporting. Past PDFs and Zoom recordings are archived going back to 2019.\n\n5) Special Workshops (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/trainings/special-workshops) — One-off topical workshops. An example documented workshop is the Cost Allowability workshop held December 9, 2022, with presentations from Farin Kamangar, Gillian Silver, Becca Steiner, Lucy Manyara, and Shamon Shine-Lee.\n\n6) Test Prep (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/trainings/test-prep) — Study materials to prepare ORA staff for the Research Administrators Certification Council (RACC) credentials: CRA® (Certified Research Administrator), CPRA® (Certified Pre-Award Research Administrator), and CFRA® (Certified Financial Research Administrator). RACC website: https://www.cra-cert.org/. Fifteen chapter-based PDF study guides are provided.\n\n7) Trainings Outside ORA (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/trainings/msu-trainings-outside-ora) — Pointers to research-relevant trainings offered by other MSU units, including the ASCEND and RCMI Fall 2023 Faculty Development Opportunities newsletter.\n\nORA training coordinators and frequent presenters include Dr. Farin Kamangar (MD, PhD, CRA, CPRA, CFRA — Associate Vice President for Research), Gillian Silver (MPH, CPH, CRA, CPRA, CFRA), Ryan Mobley (CRA, CFRA, CPRA), and Rebecca (Becca) Steiner.
